## Design

### 2026-10-21 – I designed the schematic based on the tutorial however I put my own touches on it. I started of by changing the piano key footprint for the capacitive keys into my own, unique footprint. I also decide

**3h**

I designed the schematic based on the tutorial however I put my own touches on it. I started of by changing the piano key footprint for the capacitive keys into my own, unique footprint. I also decided to the 10 capacitive keys instead of 7, 2 switches instead of 3, and no slides because those were a bit out of my budget. It's going well so far, I plan on locking in on the next session and making it at least like 4 hours or something!

### 2026-10-22 – ![Screenshot 2026-10-23 at 9.11.20 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/fd9abd3a5c82a097d3c4005885001ccb3ce92894453d4c35d2c41d84ae0ef429.png)

**7h**

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 at 9.11.20 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/fd9abd3a5c82a097d3c4005885001ccb3ce92894453d4c35d2c41d84ae0ef429.png)

![Screenshot 2026-10-23 at 9.10.43 PM](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/qTtidBuXeN0WTgEZedL39OkEOO1J2MXX/d89b62b3ecbfe5eb50147590f172423f2a76efa54d4cc89306d74cc72707b08e.png)

I completely rerouted the pcb in order or use the rotary knob's click function. I also created some firmware based on the template that was in the example. I actually locked in this session like I wanted to. I also updated the schematic in order to account for the rotary knob's click function. The firmware makes it so that twisting clockwise increases volume, counter clockwise decreases volume, and clicking it plays/pauses. I have no experience coding so I can't wait until I actually get the board so that I can test to see if my firmware works. Coding it was surprisingly easier and took much less time than I though, most of the time went into the actual routing of the PCB.
